title: Information disclosure, method of payment, and takeover premiums

rival_explanations: the lower premium in private offers reflects that only public offers can be oversubscribed (pro-rata tender-option value), not the absence of disclosure
the higher cash premium compensates target shareholders for a relative personal capital-gains tax disadvantage rather than conveying information
the superior target performance in all-cash offers reflects control/synergy transfer and is limited to control-oriented transactions

data_sources.name: CAC (Compagnie des Agents de Change) weekly stock-return data tapes, 1982 and 1984 versions (Paris forward and spot markets, 1967-1982), plus the CAC tape maintained since 1977 covering all officially listed securities incl. delisted

analyses.label: Table 3 - Average abnormal stock returns to TARGET firms, by offer category (successful/unsuccessful public tender offers for control, private tender offers for control, minority buyouts)

dv.name: target firm abnormal stock return
dv.measure: market-model-adjusted abnormal stock return (including dividends) over the event window, based on return observations from week a-52 through e+52 with orthogonal event-period dummies (eq. 2)
dv.source: Hand-collected from CAC bulletins / CAC data tapes

analyses.label: Table 4 - Average abnormal stock returns to BIDDER firms, by offer category
analyses.sample: bidder firms in the four offer categories (52 successful + 18 unsuccessful public bidders, etc.)

dv.name: bidder firm abnormal stock return
dv.measure: market-model-adjusted abnormal stock return (including dividends) over the event window (event parameters y1-y6), based on return observations week a-52 through e+52
dv.source: Hand-collected from CAC bulletins / CAC data tapes

analyses.label: Table 5 - Mean/median offer premiums and abnormal returns in successful all-cash public tender offers before (1/66-12/69) vs after (1/70-12/82) the January 1970 disclosure-regulation change, and private tender offers (1/72-12/82)
analyses.shock_or_instrument: January 1970 change in French disclosure regulations
analyses.sample: N=13 public offers 1/66-12/69, N=34 public offers 1/70-12/82, N=93 private offers 1/72-12/82

dv.name: offer premium (three components) and abnormal stock returns
dv.measure: premium over pre-offer price (P - P_{a-8})/P_{a-8}; premium over post-expiration price (P - P_{e+8})/P_{e+8}; total offer-induced target revaluation (P_{e+8} - P_{a-8})/P_{a-8}; and target/bidder abnormal returns

key_ivs.name: 1970 disclosure regulation (pre vs post)
key_ivs.measure: offers partitioned by whether they occurred before (1966-1969) or after (1970-1982) the January 1970 change in disclosure regulations

analyses.label: Table 6 - Annual average (median) offer premiums by year, 1966-1982
analyses.sample: 47 successful cash public tender offers for publicly traded French targets, 1966-1982

key_ivs.name: offer year
key_ivs.measure: annual grouping of offers 1966-1982 (period without vs with disclosure regulations)

analyses.label: Table 7 - Cross-sectional OLS regressions of offer premiums (Panel I) and abnormal returns (Panel II) on offer characteristics, cash tender offers for control
analyses.shock_or_instrument: January 1970 change in French disclosure regulations (D_70 dummy)

dv.name: offer premium components and abnormal stock returns

key_ivs.name: D_70 (post-1970 disclosure regulation dummy)

key_ivs.measure: dummy indicating a private (vs public) tender offer

controls.name: ln V_T (natural log of target total equity value)
F_h (fraction of target shares held by bidder before the offer)
F' (fraction of target shares tendered/purchased proxy)

analyses.label: Table 8 - Comparison of mean/median offer premiums and abnormal returns in all-cash (N=34) vs all-stock (N=31) public tender offers for control after 1970
analyses.sample: 34 all-cash and 31 all-stock public tender offers for control, 1970-1982

dv.name: offer premium components and abnormal returns
dv.measure: premium over pre-offer price, premium over post-expiration price, total offer-induced target revaluation, and abnormal stock returns

key_ivs.name: method of payment (cash vs securities/stock)
key_ivs.measure: partition into all-cash offers vs all-stock (securities-exchange) offers; a securities offer pays with bidder stocks and/or bonds
